Sam R.: Customer report (INC-4321) — structured/json-mode output failing to parse on their client. They see JSONDecodeError when invoice_notes contains a backslash + newline and we're streaming the response.

Sam R.: Captured streamed chunks from the model (raw):
```
chunk1: "{\"invoice_id\":\"inv_123\",\"invoice_notes\":\"Payment received on 2024-03-15\\"
chunk2: "nFollow-up required.\",\"amount\":100}"
```

Sam R.: When joined, the sequence becomes an actual newline within the JSON string (unescaped) and the client's JSON parser fails.

support-bot: Created ticket <https://support.redwood.ai/t/INC-4321|INC-4321> :ticket:

Meera K.: can you share request_id, model, structured flags + whether customer used streaming? :eyes:

Sam R.: request_id: req_0a1b2c3d  model: gpt-infer-v1  structured_mode: true  streaming: true  SDK: node@2.3.0

Alex P.: sounds like a chunk-boundary escape issue. If a chunk ends with a single backslash (\\) and the next chunk starts with n it looks like a 
 sequence — if we don't re-escape across chunk boundaries the final JSON has an actual newline.

Alex P.: minimal repro (server-side streaming):
```
// chunk sequence (literal bytes)
1: "{\"invoice_notes\":\"abc\\"
2: "nend\"}"
// joined -> "{\"invoice_notes\":\"abc\nend\"}"
// JSON parser sees an actual newline inside a string -> error
```

Ingrid (Billing): Is the source text containing a real newline or the literal `\n`? If they pasted multi-line text it should be escaped as `\\n`.

Sam R.: Customer pasted a note with a line break in the UI; they expected the model to produce escaped `\n`, but because streaming split the escape it's broken.

Diana S.: repro locally by enabling streaming and forcing small chunk sizes:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-infer-v1","structured_mode":true,"stream":true,"prompt":"invoice"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Logs: JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 34 (char 33)

Diana S.: temporary workarounds we've given the customer:
- set `stream` to `false` (non-streaming responses preserve full escapes)
- pre-encode invoice_notes (base64) then decode after parsing
- sanitize/prefix trailing backslashes on the client (replace `\` with `\\`)

Alex P.: adding to eng-runtime backlog. Short-term mitigation we can implement: treat trailing backslash at end-of-chunk as an escape-in-progress and buffer it until the next chunk (so we don't emit a dangling backslash). I'll open a patch PR.

Meera K.: assigning to @Alex P. and @Diana S. for repro + patch. Marking support:high and notifying CSM to give the customer the workaround options.

Sam R.: thanks — I'll update the customer and paste their exact raw output as soon as I have it. :thumbsup:
